items.title: Flag-variety twisted differential operators and their modules
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the published group and sheaf
suppliers. Let $G$ be a connected simply connected complex semisimple affine
algebraic group, $B\supseteq T$ a Borel subgroup and maximal torus,
$X=G/B$, $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}G$,
$\mathfrak h=\operatorname{Lie}T$, and $\Phi^+$ the positive roots selected by
$B$. Write $\rho=\frac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha$. All schemes are over
$\mathbb C$. For an integral weight $\eta$, $\mathcal O_X(\eta)$ denotes the
$G$-equivariant line bundle $G\times^B\mathbb C_\eta$ with fiber character
$\eta$ at $eB$.

The infinitesimal $G$-action gives an anchor
$$a_X:\mathcal L_X:=\mathcal O_X\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathfrak g\longrightarrow T_X,\qquad f\otimes x\longmapsto f x_X.$$
Give $\mathcal L_X$ the action-algebroid bracket
$$[f\otimes x,g\otimes y]=fg\otimes[x,y]+f x_X(g)\otimes y-g y_X(f)\otimes x.$$
Its kernel $\mathfrak b_X=\ker a_X$ is the isotropy Lie-algebra bundle; at
$gB$ its fiber is $\operatorname{Ad}(g)\mathfrak b$.

For any $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$, the character $\kappa+\rho$ of
$\mathfrak b$ (zero on $\mathfrak n^+$) transports to an
$\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\chi^X_{\kappa+\rho}:\mathfrak b_X\to\mathcal O_X$.
The transport is independent of the representative $g$ of $gB$, since a
character is invariant under the adjoint action of $B$. The action-algebroid
enveloping sheaf $\mathcal U_X(\mathfrak g)$ is generated by $\mathcal O_X$
and $\mathcal L_X$ with the displayed bracket and
$$[x,f]=x_X(f),\qquad x\in\mathcal L_X,\ f\in\mathcal O_X.$$
Define the sheaf of twisted differential operators
$$\mathcal D_\kappa:=\mathcal U_X(\mathfrak g)/\bigl(\xi-\chi^X_{\kappa+\rho}(\xi):\xi\in\mathfrak b_X\bigr).$$
Its order filtration assigns order zero to $\mathcal O_X$ and order at most
one to the image of $\mathcal L_X$. A TDO means a filtered
$\mathcal O_X$-ring with $F_0=\mathcal O_X$, associated graded
$\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}T_X$, and first-order commutator equal to
the anchor; the well-definedness and PBW properties of $\mathcal D_\kappa$
are proved in [[lem-pa36-flag-tdo-pbw-and-twist]]. A left
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-module below is required to be quasi-coherent as an
$\mathcal O_X$-module.

For $z\in Z(U(\mathfrak g))$, let $\operatorname{pr}(z)\in U(\mathfrak h)$ be
the Harish–Chandra projection along the chosen triangular decomposition, and
put
$$\chi_\kappa(z)=\operatorname{pr}(z)(\kappa-\rho).$$
This is the shifted central character: the Harish–Chandra isomorphism makes it
$W$-invariant in $\kappa$. Define
$$A_\kappa=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\kappa.$$
The regularity convention is **antidominant** when
$\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle\notin\mathbb Z_{>0}$ for each positive
root $\alpha$, and **regular** when
$\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle\ne0$ for every root. For complex weights,
$\mathbb Z_{>0}$ means the positive real integers; no order on arbitrary
complex numbers is used.

items.title: Complex-weight separation of Harish-Chandra characters
items.statement:
Let $E$ be the real span of a finite reduced crystallographic root system
$\Phi$, with chosen positive roots $\Phi^+$, simple roots
$\Delta=\{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r\}$, Weyl group $W$ and root lattice
$Q=\sum_i\mathbb Z\alpha_i$. Extend the pairing complex linearly to
$E_\mathbb C$. For $\kappa\in E_\mathbb C$, call $\kappa$ antidominant if
$\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle\notin\mathbb Z_{>0}$ for every
$\alpha\in\Phi^+$, and regular if
$\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle\ne0$ for every root. Then
$$\kappa-w\kappa\notin Q_+\setminus\{0\}\qquad(w\in W)$$
for antidominant $\kappa$, and
$$\kappa-w\kappa\notin Q_+\qquad(w\ne1)$$
when $\kappa$ is also regular. Here
$Q_+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$.

items.title: Global sections on module sheaves have ordinary sheaf cohomology as derived functors
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(X,\mathscr A)$ be a topological space with
a sheaf of unital rings (not necessarily commutative), and let
$\operatorname{Mod}(\mathscr A)$ be the category of sheaves of left
$\mathscr A$-modules. Then this category has enough injectives, every
injective $\mathscr A$-module sheaf is flasque as an underlying sheaf of
abelian groups, and for every $\mathscr A$-module sheaf $M$ the right-derived
functors of global sections in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathscr A)$ satisfy
$$R^q\Gamma_{\operatorname{Mod}(\mathscr A)}(X,M) \cong H^q(X,M)\qquad(q\ge0),$$
where the right side is ordinary sheaf cohomology of the underlying abelian
sheaf.

items.title: Cech cohomology of line bundles on the projective line
items.statement:
For $d\in\mathbb Z$, let $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(d)$ have standard
frames $e_0,e_1$ on $U_0=\{x\ne0\}$ and $U_1=\{y\ne0\}$ with
$e_1=z^d e_0$ on the overlap, where $z=y/x$ and $w=1/z$. Then
$$\dim H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(d))=\max(d+1,0),\qquad \dim H^1(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(d))=\max(-d-1,0),$$
and $H^q=0$ for $q\ge2$. For $d\ge0$, the global sections on $U_0$ are
the polynomials of degree at most $d$; for $d\le-2$, $H^1$ has Laurent
basis $z^{d+1},z^{d+2},\ldots,z^{-1}$.

items.title: The principal nilpotent Borel orbit by height elimination
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the setup of
[[def-complex-semisimple-algebraic-group-borel-and-flag-variety]]. For each
simple root $\alpha_i$ choose a nonzero root vector $e_i\in\mathfrak g_{\alpha_i}$
and put $e=\sum_i e_i$. Write
$\mathfrak n^+_j=\bigoplus_{\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)=j}\mathfrak g_\alpha$.
Then
$$B\cdot e=\left\{\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}c_\alpha e_\alpha\in\mathfrak n^+: c_{\alpha_i}\ne0\text{ for every simple root }\alpha_i\right\},$$
where one nonzero $e_\alpha\in\mathfrak g_\alpha$ is fixed for each positive
root. The right side is independent of the choices of those root vectors.

items.title: Quasicoherent modules are filtered unions of coherent subsheaves and cohomology commutes with these colimits
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X=G/B$ be the projective flag variety of
[[def-complex-semisimple-algebraic-group-borel-and-flag-variety]], and let
$\mathcal M$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. Then $\mathcal M$ is
the filtered union of its coherent $\mathcal O_X$-submodules. If
$\mathcal M=\varinjlim_j\mathcal F_j$ is any filtered colimit of
quasi-coherent modules, then for every $q\ge0$ the canonical map
$$\varinjlim_j H^q(X,\mathcal F_j)\longrightarrow H^q(X,\mathcal M)$$
is an isomorphism.

items.title: PBW and integral line-bundle twisting for flag TDOs
items.statement:
Use $X$, $\mathfrak g$, $\mathfrak b_X$, and $\mathcal D_\kappa$ from
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. For every $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ the
isotropy relations generate a two-sided ideal and define a TDO satisfying
$$F_0\mathcal D_\kappa=\mathcal O_X,\qquad \operatorname{gr}\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}T_X.$$
If $\eta\in X^*(T)$ is integral, then
$$\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Diff}\bigl(\mathcal O_X(\kappa+\rho)\bigr) \quad(\kappa+\rho\text{ integral}),\qquad \mathcal D_{-\rho}=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_X),$$
and tensoring by $\mathcal O_X(\eta)$ defines an equivalence between left
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules and left $\mathcal D_{\kappa+\eta}$-modules.

items.title: Normality of the nilpotent cone and Springer functions
items.statement:
Assume the setup of [[def-complex-semisimple-algebraic-group-borel-and-flag-variety]]
and the Axiom of Choice. Let $N\subseteq\mathfrak g$ be the nilpotent cone
with its reduced coordinate ring from
[[lem-the-nilpotent-central-fiber-is-a-reduced-integral-domain]], and let
$\mu:T^*X\to N$ be the Springer moment map. Then $N$ is normal, $\mu$ is
proper and birational, and pullback induces a graded algebra isomorphism
$$\mathbb C[N]\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(T^*X,\mathcal O_{T^*X}).$$

items.title: Partial-flag twist and local product decomposition
items.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a simple root, $P_\alpha$ its minimal parabolic,
$Y=G/P_\alpha$, and $p_\alpha:X=G/B\to Y$. Let
$\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ satisfy $\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0$.
The restriction of $\kappa$ to $\mathfrak p_\alpha$ that is zero on root
spaces is a Lie algebra character. Define the partial-flag TDO
$\mathcal D^{\alpha}_{\kappa-\rho}$ on $Y$ as the action-algebroid quotient
whose isotropy character is this restriction of $\kappa$; the subscript
$\kappa-\rho$ uses the convention that a TDO parameter $\nu$ has isotropy
character $\nu+\rho$. For a quasicoherent left
$\mathcal D^{\alpha}_{\kappa-\rho}$-module $N$, define $p_\alpha^\dagger N$
on a Zariski product chart $p_\alpha^{-1}(U)\cong U\times\mathbb P^1$ to be
the ordinary inverse-image module $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}\boxtimes N|_U$: relative vector fields differentiate the first factor, and base operators act on the second. Its underlying sheaf is $\mathcal O_X\otimes_{p_\alpha^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}p_\alpha^{-1}N$; the differential transition maps are induced by the chain rule under changes of the $P_\alpha$-torsor section. Then
these local modules glue to a quasicoherent left
$\mathcal D_{\kappa-\rho}$-module, and tensoring by $\mathcal O_X(\rho)$
turns it into a left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module. The restriction of
$\mathcal O_X(\rho)$ to each $p_\alpha$-fiber is
$\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)$.

For a torsor section $s:U\to G$, the product chart used below is the
commutative square whose top arrow is $\Phi_s(u,qB)=s(u)qB$:

```tikzcd
U\times P_\alpha/B \arrow[r,"\Phi_s"] \arrow[d,"\mathrm{pr}_1"'] & p_\alpha^{-1}(U) \arrow[d,"p_\alpha"] \\
U \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}_U"'] & U
```

The left vertical map is projection, and the bottom map is identity. The
torsor section makes $\Phi_s$ an isomorphism; the equality
$p_\alpha\circ\Phi_s=\mathrm{pr}_1$ verifies commutativity. The diagram
records the local chart only; the PBW and gluing arguments below prove the
TDO identifications.

items.title: Global sections of twisted differential operators on the flag variety
items.statement:
Assume the setup of [[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]] and the Axiom of
Choice. For every complex $\kappa$, the infinitesimal action on
$\mathcal D_\kappa$ induces a filtered algebra isomorphism
$$A_\kappa=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\kappa \xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X,\mathcal D_\kappa),$$
where $\chi_\kappa(z)=\operatorname{pr}(z)(\kappa-\rho)$. No dominance,
regularity, or integrality condition is imposed on $\kappa$.

items.title: Global sections and localization at a fixed infinitesimal character
items.statement:
Fix $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ and $A_\kappa$, $\mathcal D_\kappa$ as in
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. By
[[thm-pa36-global-twisted-differential-operators]], the sheaf
$\mathcal D_\kappa$ is a right $A_\kappa$-module by multiplication by global
sections, and $\Gamma(X,-)$ takes values in left $A_\kappa$-modules through
the infinitesimal action. Define
$$\operatorname{Loc}_\kappa(V):=\mathcal D_\kappa\otimes_{A_\kappa}V, \qquad V\in A_\kappa\text{-}\mathbf{Mod},$$
where the tensor product is the sheaf tensor product. Define
$\Gamma_\kappa(M):=\Gamma(X,M)$ for a quasi-coherent left
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-module $M$. Localization is right exact as a tensor
functor. The next item proves the adjunction and verifies that these
constructions land in the stated categories.

items.title: Ample translation maps split by central-character separation
items.statement:
Let $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ and let $\eta$ be a sufficiently dominant
integral weight, so that $L_\eta=\mathcal O_X(-\eta)$ is ample. Put
$V_\eta=\Gamma(X,L_\eta)^*$, the finite-dimensional irreducible
representation of highest weight $\eta$. For any quasi-coherent left
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-module $M$, the natural coevaluation map
$$M\longrightarrow M\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}L_\eta\otimes_{\mathbb C}V_\eta$$
is a split injection of sheaves of complex vector spaces when $\kappa$ is
antidominant. The natural evaluation map
$$M\otimes_{\mathbb C}V_\eta^*\longrightarrow M\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}L_\eta$$
is a split surjection of such sheaves when $\kappa$ is regular
antidominant. The maps and their splittings commute with the diagonal
$U(\mathfrak g)$-actions and are natural in $M$. The tensor factors
$L_\eta,V_\eta$ carry their specified $G$-linearizations; no $B$-action on
arbitrary $M$ is assumed. The splittings need not be $\mathcal O_X$-linear.
These sheaf splittings suffice for the induced split maps on cohomology.

items.title: Localization is left adjoint to global sections
items.statement:
For every $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$,
$\operatorname{Loc}_\kappa:A_\kappa\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}\to
\operatorname{QCoh}(X,\mathcal D_\kappa)$ is left adjoint to
$\Gamma_\kappa:\operatorname{QCoh}(X,\mathcal D_\kappa)\to
A_\kappa\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}$.

items.title: Antidominant twists are D-affine and regular ones are conservative
items.statement:
Assume the flag-variety setup of
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. If $\kappa$ is antidominant, then every
quasi-coherent left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module $M$ satisfies
$$H^i(X,M)=0\qquad(i>0).$$
If $\kappa$ is also regular, then $\Gamma(X,M)=0$ implies $M=0$. The
antidominance and regularity conditions are independent hypotheses; regularity
alone does not imply the vanishing assertion.

items.title: The unit V to Gamma Loc_kappa(V) is an isomorphism for antidominant twists
items.statement:
For antidominant $\kappa$ and every left $A_\kappa$-module $V$, the unit of
the adjunction in [[lem-pa36-localization-adjunction]] is an isomorphism
$$V\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X,\operatorname{Loc}_\kappa V).$$

items.title: The singular antidominant Serre quotient
items.statement:
Let $\kappa$ be antidominant, not necessarily regular, and let
$$\Gamma=\Gamma_\kappa:\operatorname{QCoh}(X,\mathcal D_\kappa) \longrightarrow A_\kappa\text{-}\mathbf{Mod},\qquad K=\ker\Gamma.$$
Then $K$ is a Serre subcategory and the induced functors give an equivalence
of abelian categories
$$\operatorname{QCoh}(X,\mathcal D_\kappa)/K \simeq A_\kappa\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}.$$
The quotient has representatives precisely among the quasicoherent
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules that are generated by global sections and have no
nonzero quasicoherent $\mathcal D_\kappa$-submodule with zero global sections.
No equivalence with the whole $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module category is asserted
without regularity.

items.title: Regular antidominant Beilinson–Bernstein localization
items.statement:
Assume the setup of [[def-pa36-global-sections-and-localization]]. If
$\kappa$ is regular antidominant, then
$$\operatorname{Loc}_\kappa:A_\kappa\text{-}\mathbf{Mod} \rightleftarrows\operatorname{QCoh}(X,\mathcal D_\kappa):\Gamma_\kappa$$
are inverse equivalences between all left $A_\kappa$-modules and all
quasi-coherent left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules. The equivalence restricts to
finitely generated $A_\kappa$-modules and coherent $\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules.
It does not assert that $\Gamma$ is faithful for a fixed non-antidominant
representative of a regular central character. Here a coherent
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-module means a module locally finitely presented over the
sheaf of rings $\mathcal D_\kappa$; its local noetherianity is part of the
proof below.

items.title: The integral regular localization equivalence restricts to Category O
items.statement:
Let $\kappa$ be integral, regular and antidominant. Define the **exact
central-character subcategory**
$$\mathcal O_{\chi_\kappa}^{\mathrm{exact}} =\{V\in\mathcal O:(\ker\chi_\kappa)V=0\}.$$
A **strongly $B$-equivariant coherent $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module** means a
coherent left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module with a rational $B$-linearization
whose differential is the action-algebroid action and whose action is
compatible with the $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module structure. Then
$\operatorname{Loc}_\kappa$ and $\Gamma_\kappa$ restrict to inverse
equivalences between $\mathcal O_{\chi_\kappa}^{\mathrm{exact}}$ and these
strongly $B$-equivariant coherent modules.

The exact subcategory is distinct from the generalized-character block, where
each vector is killed by some power of $\ker\chi_\kappa$; the theorem does not
identify the whole generalized block with $B$-equivariant coherent modules.

items.title: Relative rank-one classification of the singular differential kernel
items.statement:
Assume the complex flag-variety setup, including the Axiom of Choice, of
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. On $Z=\mathbb P^1$ put
$L=\mathcal O_Z(-1)$, $D=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_Z)$ and
$D_0=\operatorname{Diff}(L)$. Form $E=D_0\otimes_{\mathcal O_Z}L$, using
the right $\mathcal O_Z$-action on $D_0$. Evaluation gives
$$E/D_0\Gamma(Z,E)\cong L.$$
Every quasi-coherent $D_0$-module $Q$ with $\Gamma(Z,Q)=0$ has the canonical
form
$$Q\cong L\otimes_{\mathbb C}\Gamma(Z,L^{-1}\otimes Q),$$
with trivial $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-action on the second factor.

For any commutative $\mathbb C$-algebra $R$, the same classification holds
for quasi-coherent modules over the vertical ring $D_{0,R}$ on
$\mathbb P^1_R$: its kernel modules are exactly
$L_R\otimes_R N$ for $R$-modules $N$. This form commutes with every scalar
extension $R\to R'$. If $R$ is noetherian, coherence over $D_{0,R}$ is
equivalent to finite generation of $N$ over $R$. Scalar extension here
concerns only the vertical ring and a central base ring; it makes no claim
about transporting arbitrary base derivations.

More generally let $U$ be a smooth affine complex variety and let $A$ be a
TDO on $U$. For the projection $r:Z\times U\to U$, a coherent
$(D_0\boxtimes A)$-module $Q$ satisfies $R^q r_*Q=0$ for $q>0$; moreover
$r_*Q=0$ if and only if the evaluation isomorphism is
$$Q\cong L\boxtimes N,\qquad N=r_*(L^{-1}\otimes Q),$$
where $N$ is a unique coherent $A$-module. Here the ordinary differential
inverse image has underlying sheaf $\mathcal O_Z\boxtimes N$ and relative
vector fields differentiate its $\mathcal O_Z$ factor. These isomorphisms
are natural in all commuting base differential operators. Consequently they
glue over locally trivial $\mathbb P^1$-bundles with compatible product TDO
charts and line bundle restricting to $L$, as in
[[lem-pa36-partial-flag-twist-product]].

items.title: The singular simple-parabolic kernel on the flag variety
items.statement:
Let $\kappa$ be antidominant and let $\alpha$ be a simple root with
$\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0$. Put
$p_\alpha:X=G/B\to X_\alpha=G/P_\alpha$, a Zariski-locally trivial
$\mathbb P^1$-bundle, and let $\rho=\frac12\sum_{\beta\in\Phi^+}\beta$.
Use the partial TDO $\mathcal D^{\alpha}_{\kappa-\rho}$ and pullback module
$p_\alpha^\dagger N$ defined in
[[lem-pa36-partial-flag-twist-product]]. For every coherent
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-module $M$:

1. $R^q p_{\alpha*}M=0$ for every $q>0$;
2. $p_{\alpha*}M=0$ if and only if there is a coherent
   $\mathcal D^{\alpha}_{\kappa-\rho}$-module $N$ with
   $$M\cong\mathcal O_X(\rho)\otimes p_\alpha^\dagger N,$$
   where $N\cong p_{\alpha*}(\mathcal O_X(-\rho)\otimes M)$; this determines $N$ up to canonical isomorphism.

items.title: Exact twisted associated bundles and simple-parabolic descent
items.statement:
Assume the complex simply connected semisimple setup, including the Axiom of
Choice, of [[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. Let $S$ be $B$ or a minimal
parabolic $P_\alpha$, put $Y=G/S$, and let $\tau$ be an
$\operatorname{Ad}(S)$-invariant character of $\mathfrak s$. A
**twisted $(\mathfrak g,S)$-module of twist $\tau$** means a vector space
$H$ with a Lie representation $\pi:\mathfrak g\to\operatorname{End}H$ and
a rational $S$-representation $r$, such that
$$d r(x)=\pi(x)+\tau(x)\operatorname{id}_H\quad(x\in\mathfrak s),\qquad r(s)\pi(A)r(s)^{-1}=\pi(\operatorname{Ad}(s)A).$$
The weight $\tau$ can be complex; no rational character $s\mapsto s^\tau$
is presumed. Define $\mathcal A^S_\tau$ by the action-algebroid quotient on
$Y$ with isotropy character $\tau$, and define
$$\mathsf E^S_\tau(H)=G\times^S(H,r).$$
For infinite-dimensional rational modules, this is the associated
quasi-coherent sheaf, locally $\mathcal O_Y\otimes_{\mathbb C}H$.
Then $\mathsf E^S_\tau$ is an exact functor to quasi-coherent
$\mathcal A^S_\tau$-modules. For $S=B$,
$\mathcal A^B_{\kappa+\rho}=\mathcal D_\kappa$.

If $V$ is a finite-dimensional rational $G$-module, use the diagonal Lie
and $S$ actions on $H\otimes V$. Then
$$\mathsf E^S_\tau(H\otimes V)\cong \mathsf E^S_\tau(H)\otimes_{\mathbb C}V,$$
where the differential action on the right acts only on the first factor:
constant vectors in $V$ are horizontal. In particular, with
$M(\lambda)=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}\mathbb C_\lambda$,
$$\mathsf E^B_{\kappa+\rho}(M(-\kappa-\rho))\cong\mathcal D_\kappa, \qquad \mathsf E^B_{\kappa+\rho}(M(-\kappa))\cong \mathcal D_\kappa\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_X(\rho).$$
In these formulas the rational $B$-action is the adjoint action on the
induced module with its highest vector of twisted weight $0$ or $\rho$,
respectively; the tensor product on the last right-hand side uses the right
$\mathcal O_X$-action on $\mathcal D_\kappa$.

Finally suppose $\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0$ and $H$ is twisted
$(\mathfrak g,P_\alpha)$ of twist $\kappa$. Let
$N=\mathsf E^{P_\alpha}_\kappa(H)$, a module over the partial TDO
$\mathcal D^\alpha_{\kappa-\rho}$ of
[[lem-pa36-partial-flag-twist-product]]. Restrict its rational action to
$B$ and tensor that rational action by the integral character $\rho$;
with unchanged $\pi$ this makes $H$ twisted of twist $\kappa+\rho$.
For this latter structure,
$$\mathsf E^B_{\kappa+\rho}(H)\cong \mathcal O_X(\rho)\otimes p_\alpha^\dagger N.$$
Here $p_\alpha^\dagger$ is ordinary differential inverse image, with local
underlying sheaf $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}\boxtimes N$.

items.title: A fixed singular Verma chain with globally generated final bundle
items.statement:
Assume the complex flag-variety setup, including the Axiom of Choice, of
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. Let $\kappa$ be antidominant, put
$$\Phi_\kappa=\{\beta\in\Phi:\langle\kappa,\beta^\vee\rangle=0\}, \qquad J=\Delta\cap\Phi_\kappa,$$
and assume $J$ is a simple system for the full zero-root subsystem
$\Phi_\kappa$. Choose a reduced expression
$w_J=s_{\alpha_N}\cdots s_{\alpha_1}$ for the longest element of $W_J$.
Set $\mu_0=\rho$, $\mu_j=s_{\alpha_j}\mu_{j-1}$, and
$$H_j=M(-\kappa-\rho+\mu_j),\qquad \mathcal E_j=\mathsf E^B_{\kappa+\rho}(H_j),$$
using the exact twisted associated-bundle functor in
[[lem-pa36-twisted-associated-bundle-and-parabolic-descent]]. The rational
$B$-action has highest-vector weight $\mu_j$. Then there are embeddings
$$H_N\subseteq\cdots\subseteq H_0,\qquad \mathcal E_N\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathcal E_0 =\mathcal D_\kappa\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_X(\rho).$$
For each $j$, a coherent module $N_j$ over
$\mathcal D^{\alpha_j}_{\kappa-\rho}$ satisfies
$$\mathcal E_{j-1}/\mathcal E_j\cong \mathcal O_X(\rho)\otimes p_{\alpha_j}^\dagger N_j.$$
Furthermore $\mathcal E_N$ is generated as a $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module by
finitely many global sections: for a finite-dimensional rational irreducible
$G$-module $V$ of highest weight $\rho$ there is a surjection
$$\mathcal D_\kappa\otimes_{\mathbb C}V\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal E_N,$$
with horizontal constant $V$-factor. The sequence of roots depends only on
the chosen reduced expression in $W_J$, not on any later module to which
the chain is applied. When $J$ is empty, $N=0$ and the same assertions hold
with $H_N=H_0$.

items.title: Kashiwara's singular parabolic kernel filtration
items.statement:
Let $\kappa$ be antidominant, let
$$J=\{\alpha_i\in\Delta:\langle\kappa,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle=0\},$$
and assume its full zero-root subsystem is generated by $J$. For each
$\alpha\in J$, write $p_\alpha:X\to X_\alpha=G/P_\alpha$ for the simple
parabolic projection. Then there exists a finite sequence
$\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_N\in J$ such that for every coherent
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-module $M$ the following are equivalent:

1. $\Gamma(X,M)=0$;
2. there is a finite coherent filtration
   $$M=M_0\supseteq M_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq M_N=0$$
   with $p_{\alpha_j*}(M_{j-1}/M_j)=0$ for every $j$.

The sequence is one choice, not asserted to be unique; zero successive
quotients are permitted.

title: Beilinson–Bernstein Localization and Category O: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A positive integral SL2 twist is regular but not D-affine
items.statement:
Regularity of $\kappa$ alone implies that $\Gamma(X,-)$ is exact and
conservative for $\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules.

items.title: The SL2 flag charts realize the stated rho shift
items.statement:
Let $G=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb C)$, $X=G/B\cong\mathbb P^1$, and use the
repository basis
$$h=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad e=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad f=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.$$
Let $\rho$ satisfy $\rho(h)=1$. For an integer $c$, set
$\kappa=c\rho$ and $d=-c-1$. Then
$$\mathcal D_{c\rho}=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(d)).$$
On $U_0=\{x\ne0\}$ with coordinate $z=y/x$ and frame $e_0=x^d$, the
infinitesimal action is
$$e=z^2\partial_z+(c+1)z,\qquad f=-\partial_z,\qquad h=2z\partial_z+(c+1).$$
On $U_1=\{y\ne0\}$ with coordinate $w=x/y$ and frame $e_1=y^d$, it is
$$e=-\partial_w,\qquad f=w^2\partial_w+(c+1)w,\qquad h=-2w\partial_w-(c+1).$$
These formulas glue, satisfy the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ relations, and give
$\mathcal D_{-\rho}=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1})$ when
$c=-1$.

items.title: Integral line-bundle translation changes the infinitesimal character
items.statement:
For $G=\mathrm{SL}_2$, start at the singular twist $\kappa=0$ with the
nonzero $\mathcal D_0$-module $M=\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)$. Tensor by the
integral line bundle $\mathcal O_X(\rho)=\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)$. The
result is the $\mathcal D_\rho$-module $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-2)$, since
integral line-bundle translation changes the twist from $\kappa$ to
$\kappa+\rho$. The Casimir characters change from
$$\chi_0(C)=-\tfrac12\quad\text{to}\quad\chi_\rho(C)=0.$$
The translated parameter $\rho$ is not antidominant, and the translated
module still has zero global sections (indeed $\dim H^1=1$); the twist
equivalence on sheaf modules does not assert that global sections is faithful
at the translated parameter.

items.title: A point-supported SL2 module gives the shifted Verma module
items.statement:
Use $G=\mathrm{SL}_2$, $X=\mathbb P^1$, and $\kappa=c\rho$ with
$c\in\mathbb Z$. Let $x_0$ be the Borel-fixed point $z=0$ in the $U_0$
chart of [[ex-pa36-sl2-twisted-differential-operators]], and let
$\delta_{x_0}$ be the left $\mathcal D_{c\rho}$-module supported at $x_0$.
Then
$$\Gamma(X,\delta_{x_0})\cong M((c-1)\rho)=U(\mathfrak{sl}_2)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}\mathbb C_{(c-1)\rho}.$$
For the Casimir
$$C=ef+fe+\tfrac12h^2,$$
both this Verma module and the central character $\chi_{c\rho}$ have scalar
$\frac12(c^2-1)$.

items.title: At the singular SL2 twist global sections is not conservative
items.statement:
The global-sections functor is conservative for every antidominant twist,
including singular twists, and the corresponding simple-parabolic
pushforward detects every nonzero module.

items.title: Finite-dimensional sl2 modules lie in the exact integral central-character part
items.statement:
Let $G=\mathrm{SL}_2$ and $n\ge0$. The finite-dimensional irreducible
$V(n\rho)$ of highest weight $n\rho$ lies in BGG category $\mathcal O$ and
has exact central character $\chi_{(n+1)\rho}$. Since the Weyl group sends
$(n+1)\rho$ to $-(n+1)\rho$, the same character has regular antidominant
representative
$$\kappa=-(n+1)\rho.$$
The corollary [[cor-pa36-category-o-localization]] therefore localizes this
object to a coherent strongly B-equivariant $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module. The
claim concerns the **exact** central-character subcategory
$\ker\chi_\kappa\cdot V=0$. The generalized-character condition
$\forall v\ \exists N:\,(\ker\chi_\kappa)^N v=0$ is a different condition;
no equivalence for the entire generalized block is asserted.
